transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jonas Weaver, Priya Nair (Redwood); Luca Romano, Sofia Chen, Aaron Mills, Ravi Desai (Ember Tech)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick kickoff to align on activation milestones, security gating items, and pilot scope.

[00:00] Maya Patel: All right thanks everyone for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, uh Jonas and Priya are with me, Jonas is our CSM, Priya's our SE, we'll do the technical run and then hand over to CSM stuff. How's that sound?
[00:08] Luca Romano: Sounds good, thanks Maya. Hey everyone, Luca here, VP Eng at Ember. We've got Sofia and Aaron and Ravi on from platform and security.
[00:13] Sofia Chen: hi hi, thanks.
[00:15] Jonas Weaver: Hey! quick note, we set this at 52 minutes so we'll try to keep to schedule.

[00:30] Priya Nair: Great, I'll start with a quick overview of what success looks like for a pilot — usually we want to validate latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, and functional parity on a handful of prompt families. then we can talk deployment options.
[00:45] Aaron Mills: yeah for us latency is the biggest thing. If we can't get under 150ms p50 for the chat flows it's going to be tough. But cost is also material — we have a rough budget for inference.
[00:58] Maya Patel: that's helpful. Can you tell us a bit about traffic shape? concurrency, typical prompt lengths?
[01:05] Luca Romano: Mostly short chat queries, 16-48 tokens prompts typically, but sometimes longer system instructions ~200 tokens for summarization jobs. Peak concurrency is around 120 concurrent users hitting the API, but that translates to maybe 30 QPS average.
[01:20] Priya Nair: Perfect. That profile maps well to our Dedicated pools or Redwood Hosted with autoscale. For predictable p50 numbers Dedicated is safer. For cost experimentation Hosted with autoscale might be cheaper initially.
[01:35] Sofia Chen: We want private networking though — everything must go through our VPC and private subnets. On-prem is also on the table for some regulated customers.
[01:44] Maya Patel: noted. So Redwood Private (VPC package) or on-prem would be options. We'll need to share our Private deployment docs and the network requirements.

[02:05] Ravi Desai: Quick security stuff from our side: we need KMS integration for customer-managed keys, SSO via SAML, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and evidence of SOC 2. Also retention policies — some logs should be purged after X days.
[02:18] Jonas Weaver: yep that's all standard, we have SOC 2 Type II, we support external KMS, SAML/SCIM for SSO and RBAC. We'll send the compliance packet.
[02:27] Ravi Desai: okay great. Also, do you have an HSM workflow for keys? we use a cloud KMS but some teams want HSM-backed keys.
[02:34] Priya Nair: We can integrate with customer KMS. HSM-backed keys are supported via our KMS partners; we'll include integration notes and expected auth flow.

[02:50] [Timestamp jump, network noise in recording]
[03:10] Aaron Mills: on the infra side, we run EKS with AWS ALB ingress, and a private NAT for outbound. We have strict egress rules so we'll need a list of endpoints and IP ranges to allow.
[03:22] Maya Patel: we'll get the IP ranges and endpoints. For Private install you'll want to see the installer manifest; we'll share a baseline manifest for EKS.

[04:00] Priya Nair: Talk about pilot scope — suggested approach: week 1 run a functional smoke test with sample prompts, week 2 run load/latency benchmarks capturing p50/p95 and token cost, week 3 iterate on batching/quantization and re-run. That usually gives customers the data to make a Dedicated sizing decision.
[04:18] Luca Romano: Sounds pragmatic. How much setup time for Private?
[04:22] Priya Nair: Private is typically 1-2 weeks for our standard VPC-based deployment assuming we get network artifacts quickly. On-prem can be longer depending on air-gapped requirements.
[04:30] Sofia Chen: And what about the KV cache and prefix caching — does that require any special config? we do a lot of conversational state.
[04:38] Priya Nair: Good question, KV - or K V - cache is managed by the runtime; for multi-turn chat we'll surface config knobs for cache TTL per model, and we can pin model variants to reduce cold-starts. No infra changes usually, but there are tuning levers.

[05:05] Luca Romano: Is there a way to fall back to smaller models when load spikes? we want graceful degradation.
[05:11] Maya Patel: Yes, our routing policy can fallback to cheaper model variants or region-based fallbacks. We'll help define those policies as part of the pilot.

[06:00] Aaron Mills: any notes on observability? we need traces and token-level billing breakdowns for our finance team.
[06:08] Jonas Weaver: we have per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and trace hooks that integrate with Datadog or Honeycomb. We'll share dashboard templates.

[06:40] Priya Nair: Let's talk about benchmarks — we'll need a representative prompt set. Can Ember provide that?
[06:47] Sofia Chen: yes we'll put together 20-30 prompts across chat and summarization, and annotate expected outputs.
[06:54] Priya Nair: Great. Also, please include any auth flows we should exercise (service tokens, end-user SSO, etc.).

[07:10] [15:10] — (simulated timestamp to show mid-meeting) 
[15:12] Luca Romano: One more question on pricing: for Dedicated do you have committed monthly rates vs pay-as-you-go?
[15:20] Maya Patel: yes we have reserved capacity options with monthly/annual commits. I'll send a summary with example sizing and estimated unit costs based on the pilot results.
[15:29] Aaron Mills: If the pilot shows we can hit latency targets at X cost then we can fast-track procurement.

[16:00] Ravi Desai: On the compliance packet, how granular are the audit logs? do you include per-request metadata?
[16:08] Jonas Weaver: audit logs include request metadata, model version, user token id (masked), and routing decisions. We can stream logs to your SIEM or provide S3 export.

[20:00] Priya Nair: For the pilot we'll do this: 1) exchange network artifacts and credentials to set up Private trial in a dedicated VPC — this will let us measure real p50s; 2) run benchmark suite capturing latency and cost; 3) iterate on batching/caching and report. Estimated timeline 2-3 weeks end-to-end if artifacts are timely.
[20:22] Sofia Chen: timeline works if we can get the network info by next Friday.
[20:28] Maya Patel: noted, we'll expect Aaron to share infra diagram and egress rules by 2026-07-03.

[25:00] Aaron Mills: Quick operational question — how do model rollouts work? we sometimes need canaries for production.
[25:08] Priya Nair: We support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. Rollouts are configurable per-model and per-route.

[30:00] Luca Romano: Are there any gotchas for region residency — we have EU customers and we need data to stay in eu-west-1 for certain tenants.
[30:11] Maya Patel: yes we support region pinning in Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. We'll document data residency options and encryption keys per-region.

[35:00] [little cross-talk]
[35:20] Jonas Weaver: I'll be the CSM point; we'll coordinate weekly check-ins during the pilot and then a handoff cadence for production.
[35:30] Luca Romano: Good. Who will be the SE contact for the benchmark?
[35:35] Priya Nair: I'll own the benchmark and work with Aaron.

[40:00] Maya Patel: Recap and next steps: Maya to send contract summary and pricing, Priya to prepare pilot benchmark script, Aaron to share infra diagram and egress/IP list, Ravi to confirm compliance/retention asks. We'll also share the Private deployment manifest and SOC 2 packet.
[40:20] Sofia Chen: noted. We also want a 30-minute deep dive on network setup next week.
[40:25] Maya Patel: let's book that — Jonas can follow up with a calendar invite.

[45:00] Luca Romano: any blockers we foresee?
[45:06] Aaron Mills: only potential blocker is procurement timeline if dedicated capacity is chosen, but we can start pilot on Private to collect data before commit.

[46:00] Maya Patel: okay, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and set the next meeting.
[46:10] [03:10] (minor audio glitch)
[46:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: There are a few mis-hearings in product names (e.g., "K V cache" instead of KV cache), punctuation is rough. Natural speech preserved with brief filler words. Some timestamps are approximate.
